So I can't create `test_sse.py`.

I can run a python script using `run_command`.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import SSEResponse
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import asyncio

app = FastAPI()

async def event_generator():
    yield "data: hello\n\n"
    yield "data: world\n\n"

@app.get("/sse")
async def sse_endpoint():
    return SSEResponse(event_generator())

client = TestClient(app)

def test_sse():
    with client.stream("GET", "/sse") as response:
        assert response.status_code == 200
        assert response.headers["content-type"] == "text/event-stream"
        assert response.headers["cache-control"] == "no-cache"
        assert response.headers["connection"] == "keep-alive"
        assert response.headers["x-accel-buffering"] == "no"
        
        lines = response.iter_lines()
        assert next(lines).decode() == "data: hello"
        assert next(lines).decode() == ""
        assert next(lines).decode() == "data: world"
        assert next(lines).decode() == ""

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_sse()
    print("SSE test passed!")
```

Actually, `client.stream` is available in `TestClient` (which uses `httpx`).
